ai.title: read-subtree accepts empty path string
ai.summary: read-subtree tool schema updated to accept empty strings in paths array. Previously, z.string().min(1) rejected empty paths, causing errors when users passed empty strings. Now, empty strings are treated as equivalent to '.' (project root), aligning with common path resolution behavior. Affects common/src/tools/params/tool/read-subtree.ts.

eli5.text: When you ask the project-reading tool to look at a folder, leaving the path blank used to cause an error; now the tool treats a blank path the same as the main project folder, so requests that accidentally pass an empty path work instead of failing. Anyone using this tool is affected, and you would notice that previously failing requests now return the project contents normally.

ai.title: CLI 1.0.544 ships schema, search, and eval updates
ai.summary: Bumped the CLI package version from 1.0.543 to 1.0.544 in cli/release/package.json. This release consolidates several agent-runtime and sdk improvements: the code-search tool now skips hidden directories that do not exist to avoid ripgrep stderr noise, read-subtree accepts empty path strings as project-root equivalents, and tool input schemas were unified to match the spawn_agents nesting. Stream parsing also gained ordered error handling and BuffBench now logs full judge outputs plus optional DEBUG_ERROR debug files.
ai.evidence: cli/release/package.json hunk changes "version": "1.0.543" to "1.0.544"; release updates list 8 user-visible changes since 1.0.543 including code-search hidden-dir filtering, agent tool input schema unification, stream-parser error ordering fixes, read-subtree empty-path support, and BuffBench judge/debug logging additions.

eli5.text: Version 1.0.544 improves code search, makes evaluations run more reliably, and fixes small bugs that were causing error messages to appear in the wrong order. The code search tool now skips hidden directories that don\'t actually exist in your project, so you\'ll stop seeing confusing warnings about missing paths when searching through large codebases. Evaluation benchmarks now properly set up their environment by running install and build steps before testing, and they capture full error details when something goes wrong, making it easier to debug failures. You can now pass an empty path to the read-subtree command and it will default to your project root, matching the behavior you\'d expect from command line tools. Additionally, error messages from multiple tools are now grouped and presented after all tool results rather than being mixed in, which prevents confusing overlaps when several things fail at once. Upgrading gives you cleaner search results, more dependable automated testing, and clearer error reporting that follows the correct order.

ai.title: BuffBench supports multi-file eval runs and adds hard-task analysis
ai.summary: runBuffBench now accepts evalDataPaths array instead of single evalDataPath, enabling cross-repo evaluation in one pass. New analyze-task-scores.ts identifies hard tasks (score <= 7.5) from logs, while main-hard-tasks.ts runs 45 selected tasks across Codebuff, Manifold, Plane, and Saleor eval sets. Nightly and main scripts updated to use array format with consolidated repo URL reporting.

eli5.text: The system that tests the assistant against real-world coding jobs now runs across many projects at once instead of just one, so it can see how well the assistant handles tasks from programs like Codebuff, Manifold, Plane, and Saleor in a single pass. It also gains a new check that flags which tasks the assistant consistently struggles with (scoring 7.5 or lower), so developers can focus on the hardest problems. You would notice this if you looked at the test results: instead of separate runs for each project, there's now one combined report listing multiple repositories and a new section calling out the most difficult tasks.

ai.title: Fix thinking block width calculation
ai.summary: Adjusted available width calculation in `thinking-block.tsx` by increasing reserved space from 4 to 10 units. This change prevents jittery rendering of thinking blocks in the CLI interface. The fix is scoped to the CLI component logic.

eli5.text: When the CLI assistant shows its private thinking section (the indented reasoning that appears before a reply), each line is now laid out with a bit more careful spacing. Previously the system guessed that only a few characters were needed for indentation, which left the rest of the line too wide; that miscalculation made the text jitter and re-wrap as the block updated in real time. It nudges the line-width math so that the left indent and the right edge line up consistently, which is why the previously twitchy, jumping thinking block now stays steady on screen.

ai.title: Switch thinker agent to Claude Opus 4.5 and structured output
ai.summary: The `thinker` agent definition updated model to `anthropic/claude-opus-4.5` and switched `outputMode` to `structured_output` with a custom `handleSteps` generator. The agent now extracts text from the last assistant message and calls `set_output` internally, while the LLM is instructed not to call tools. The `thinker` agent is added to the default spawnable list in `createBase2`. The validation rule requiring `set_output` in `toolNames` for structured output is disabled in `DynamicAgentTemplateSchema` to allow `handleSteps` to manage the tool call without exposing it to the model.

eli5.text: A helper inside the system that works through tough problems piece by piece now uses a more powerful version of the AI that drives it, and its results are collected in a clean, machine-readable form instead of as loose text. The helper is now offered to people running the default setup. Behind the scenes, a rule that normally forces tools to be manually listed was relaxed so this helper's internal steps aren't visible to the AI writing the response. If you looked at one of these helpers in action, you wouldn't see the AI reach around for random tools; it just thinks step by step and the final answer pops out in a structured box. The more powerful AI model means the helper's reasoning tends to be a bit sharper, but the way it hands its conclusion back has quietly gotten more predictable.

ai.title: thinker-best-of-n uses <think> tags
ai.summary: Updated instructionsPrompt in `.agents/thinker/best-of-n/thinker-best-of-n.ts` to direct subagents to use `<think>` tags for reasoning. Implemented regex stripping of `<think>...</think>` content in `handleStepsDefault` and `handleStepsOpus` before passing thoughts to the selector. This ensures only the final concise response reaches the parent agent, preventing raw chain-of-thought leakage.

eli5.text: When you ask the thinker-best-of-n agent to reason deeply about your request, its subagents now wrap their inner reasoning in dedicated tags. Those hidden thoughts are stripped away before the parent agent sees them, so you only receive the subagents' final concise answers instead of their raw chain-of-thought reasoning. This change is live today in the internal agent tooling.

eli5.text: Starting today, the system's default workflow uses a smarter model called Opus to draft and refine code instead of the older Max variant. If you trigger an automated code review or complex change, you'll now get results written by Opus, which the tool picks because it produces better implementations. The number of parallel attempts the system runs has also been tuned: it now generates up to six candidate drafts instead of ten, and it starts with three in parallel by default rather than four.

eli5.text: When you ask the editor to brainstorm several alternatives at once (the 'best of n' Opus path), it now always spins up exactly 10 helper copies instead of a variable number, trims away the old prompt and instructions from the conversation before starting so only the most recent task is in context, and gives the next step your full, unfiltered edit text instead of just the tool-shaped pieces it used to carve out. If you look, you'd notice the helper agents are always 10, and the editor applies edits using the chosen alternative's complete text rather than a filtered subset. This path is live today.

ai.title: Relax setoutput tool requirement for structuredoutput mode
ai.summary: Validation logic in DynamicAgentTemplateSchema and validateAgents now permits structured_output mode without requiring set_output in toolNames. This change allows handleSteps generators to yield set_output actions even when the underlying LLM does not have direct access to the tool. The update affects agent definition parsing in common/src/types/dynamic-agent-template.ts and SDK validation in sdk/src/validate-agents.ts. Tests in agent-validation.test.ts, dynamic-agent-template-schema.test.ts, handlesteps-parsing.test.ts, and validate-agents.test.ts were updated to reflect the new permissive behavior.

eli5.text: If you build an automated assistant that is supposed to hand back a structured answer (like a form or JSON object), the software used to demand that the assistant itself have a specific "set_output" capability listed in its toolset. That requirement has now been dropped, so you can write an assistant that uses the structured-answer mode even when the assistant's own toolset does not directly include that set_output capability. This matters mainly to developers who compose these assistants with the step-by-step handling feature, since their generated steps can now yield a set_output action without first having to add set_output to the assistant's visible tools.

ai.title: Expand Forbidden error messages in admin and session APIs
ai.summary: 403 responses in admin-auth.ts and logout-all/route.ts now include specific reasons instead of generic 'Forbidden'. Admin checks return 'Forbidden - not an admin', while cross-origin logout attempts return 'Forbidden - not same origin, cannot logout all sessions'. Changes affect web/src/app/api/admin/admin-auth.ts, web/src/app/api/user/sessions/logout-all/route.ts, and web/src/lib/admin-auth.ts. Error payloads remain JSON with status 403.

eli5.text: When someone without admin privileges tries to access an admin-only area, the error message now says 'Forbidden - not an admin' instead of just 'Forbidden'. When a login attempt comes from a different website trying to log out all sessions, it now says 'Forbidden - not same origin, cannot logout all sessions' instead of the generic message. The actual blocking behavior didn't change - these users were already denied access - but the messages now explain exactly why in plain language. This affects only internal admin tools and session management, so regular users won't notice any difference.

ai.title: Clarify force push policy in knowledge.md
ai.summary: Updated `knowledge.md` to explicitly require user confirmation before using `git push --force` or `--force-with-lease` on the main branch. The policy now clarifies that a simple push request is not permission, and agents must stop and ask if a push is rejected due to diverged history. This change applies to the agent's internal knowledge base, affecting behavior across all surfaces.

eli5.text: The instructions the assistant follows internally now explicitly state that force pushing to the main branch requires direct, clear permission from you, and a regular 'please push' request does not count as that permission. If a push gets rejected because the branch has moved forward, the assistant will stop and ask you what to do instead of automatically trying a force push, which could erase other people's work. This rule is now in place and applies to every interaction today.

ai.title: CLI publish adds dependents toggle and bundled filter
ai.summary: The publish UI introduces an includeDependents toggle to visualize and include reverse dependencies in the confirmation step. Bundled agents are now filtered out of the publishable list via an isBundled flag in prebuild-agents.ts. The publish command passes allLocalAgentIds to the API client for server-side validation. SelectedChips.tsx component added to display selected agents with removal support.

eli5.text: When you go to publish your agents, you'll now see a new toggle that lets you include reverse dependencies - agents that call/spawn the ones you've selected - so the confirmation screen shows the full picture of what would be affected. Bundled agents (pre-packaged ones) no longer appear in your publish list, and the system now sends the complete set of your local agent IDs to the server so it can catch any missing dependencies before publishing. You'll also see little chip labels showing your selected agents with the ability to remove them individually.

ai.title: Prevent image content propagation to spawned subagents
ai.summary: The `executeSubagent` function in `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/handlers/tool/spawn-agent-utils.ts` now explicitly sets `content` to `undefined` when calling `loopAgentSteps`. This prevents the parent agent's image content from being automatically passed to spawned subagents. Subagents requiring image access must rely on `includeMessageHistory` rather than implicit content propagation. This change ensures cleaner separation of concerns and avoids potential context bloat or security issues related to unmanaged image data flow.

eli5.text: When an assistant spawns a helper to work on a sub-task, that helper no longer automatically receives any images the main assistant was looking at. If the helper genuinely needs to see those images, it has to request them explicitly through the includeMessageHistory option, instead of getting them by default. This went live as part of an agent runtime update that landed in a snapshot on December 8, 2025, alongside other changes like the read-subtree command accepting an empty path string and the thinker agent switching to Claude Opus 4.5. If you were watching a sub-task unfold and it previously seemed to 'just know' about an image from the parent conversation, it will now ignore that image unless the parent deliberately includes the full message history when handing off.

ai.summary: Enhanced error logging for OpenRouter requests in `web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/_post.ts` and stream handling in `web/src/llm-api/openrouter.ts`. eli5.text: The system now keeps a much more detailed paper trail when something goes wrong while talking to the upstream AI provider. If a request fails (either as a single response or while streaming tokens back to you), the logs will now record who you are, which assistant run you were on, which model you picked, and the exact error code and provider message that came back. This does not change what you see in your chat session, but it gives the people maintaining the service far more to go on when investigating why a particular request failed. The richer logging is in effect today.

ai.summary: run-agent-step.ts imports APICallError and branches error handling. Non-APICallError cases retain standard message/stack extraction. APICallError instances now log URL, request body values, status code, response headers, response body, retryability, and data. Scope limited to packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts.

eli5.text: When this software hits a problem while talking to an AI service, it now shows you far more detail about what went wrong: the exact web address it tried to reach, the data it sent, the error code the service returned, any extra response details, and whether the system will try again automatically. If the problem is a more ordinary kind of error, the message stays the same as before. You would notice this only if you run the agent runtime and it fails during an AI request, where the error log will now be much longer and more specific.

ai.title: Publish UI adds dependents toggle, isolates subagent image content
ai.summary: The 1.0.546 release ships the publish UI's includeDependents toggle for visualizing reverse dependencies during the confirmation step, alongside filtered bundled agents flagged via isBundled and server-side validation through allLocalAgentIds. Spawned subagents no longer inherit the parent's image content, executeSubagent now explicitly passes content as undefined, so subagents that need image access must rely on includeMessageHistory. Minor improvements include the documented force-push confirmation policy, the Zed scroll multiplier raised from 0.37 to 0.5, BigQuery trace insert failures now logged at warn, and richer context in error logging for OpenRouter and APICallError paths. The CLI package version in cli/release/package.json advances from 1.0.545 to 1.0.546 with no other lockfile-only changes.
ai.evidence: Commit [c0d59c83] bumps version 1.0.545 to 1.0.546 in cli/release/package.json as a release-bump. eli5.text: This release improves how you share your work and how agents behave when helping with coding tasks. The publish feature now lets you include the projects that depend on what you are sharing, so you can see the full picture before you confirm. It also hides built-in agents from the list so you only see the ones you actually want to publish. Spawned helper agents no longer inherit image content from the main conversation, keeping things cleaner and avoiding unnecessary context overflow. Force-pushing to the main branch now requires explicit confirmation, protecting your history from accidental overwrites. Scrolling feels smoother in the chat, error messages from model providers are more detailed for troubleshooting, and failed trace logging is less noisy. Upgrading gives you a safer, clearer publishing flow, better protected shared history, and more helpful diagnostic information when things go wrong.
